title: Target anatomy
view: Transverse section of the right neck at mid-SCM under a linear probe, as on ultrasound: posterior (lateral) on the image left, anterior (carotid) on the right, skin at the top.
teachingPoint: The plexus is a small cluster at the posterior border of the SCM; the needle comes in-plane from posterior, the tip in the plane just deep to that border, and the spread runs along it.
claims: Right neck in section, posterior on the left, as on ultrasound (house laterality, matches the interscalene plate).
SCM is the large superficial muscle; levator scapulae and scalenes lie deep to it (record, ultrasound).
Plexus as a small cluster at the posterior border of the SCM, deep to it (record, anatomy and ultrasound).
External jugular vein on the SCM near this level (record, anatomy).
Needle in-plane from posterior to anterior, tip in the plane just deep to the posterior border (record, steps 4-5).
Teal: spread along the posterior border, between SCM and the prevertebral fascia (record, step 6).
Labels: Sternocleidomastoid, External jugular vein, Superficial cervical plexus, Levator scapulae, Carotid.
